title: Siouan languages - Wikipedia
text: The Western Siouan languages are typically subdivided into Missouri River languages (such as Crow and Hidatsa), Mandan, Mississippi River languages (such as Dakota, Chiwere - Ho-Chunk, and Dhegihan languages), and Ohio Valley Siouan languages (Ofo, Biloxi, and Tutelo).

title: Biloxi people - Wikipedia
text: The Biloxi tribe (endonym: Tanêks (a)) are Native Americans of the Siouan-Catawban language family. When first encountered by Europeans in 1699, the Biloxi inhabited an area near the coast of the Gulf of Mexico near what is now the city of Biloxi, Mississippi.

title: Catawban languages - Wikipedia
text: The Catawban branch consists of a subset of various historical languages in the Siouan–Catawban language family, within the Appalachian Plateau and Piedmont regions of present-day Virginia and the Carolinas.

text: In the east, the language is referred to as the Siouan-Catawban. This language was the most divergent from the other Siouan tribes and is extinct today. The Siouan language once consisted of 17 dialects, many of which are either extinct or severely endangered today.

title: Biloxi Language and the Biloxi Indian Tribe
text: Language: Biloxi was a Siouan language spoken in Mississippi and Alabama. It featured SOV word order. The Biloxi tribe was devastated by a smallpox epidemic, and the survivors migrated westward and merged with the Tunica Indians, with whom they share a Louisiana reservation today.
